geometry_edits.rationale: Increase bend to strengthen the dominant spatial rule without breaking continuity.
Raise the body slightly more so the upper mass reads as a clearer hierarchy above the ground response.
Expand the carved void to improve publicness and ground-level legibility.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the continuous bent gesture so the dominant mass reads more decisively across views.
Slightly increase upper lift to improve hierarchy while preserving the compact neighborhood-scale body.
Enlarge the public void modestly so the court is more legible and usable as a ground-space figure.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent bent-and-carved mass in all four views, with a clear dominant U-like gesture, a legible central void, and a consistent orientation to the parcel. The blue access edge is answered by a visible opening/cut rather than a sealed frontage, which suits the neighborhood-living brief. The form is still somewhat box-derived and the section is not especially rich, but the spatial rules remain coherent and the mass does not visibly collide across views. It is program-plausible as compact neighborhood mixed-use/living support because it offers an active ground threshold plus a usable court/entry sequence instead of a generic closed block.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more pavilion-like and sculptural than the candidate; do not imitate its exact curving parapets.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise composition with a legible central void and an upper connector can support a neighborhood program while keeping the ground readable.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is much larger and more dispersed; candidate must stay compact and avoid becoming a campus planning diagram.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like aggregation around a courtyard can translate into a public interior court and clearer hierarchy among parts.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is boxier and more rectilinear; the candidate already has a stronger sectional gesture.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A shallow cutout and overhang can produce a strong public threshold without overcomplicating the mass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is not as horizontally extended and should not be forced into a low-slung strip condition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Long horizontal spread with a central void and folded roof logic can make a mixed-use building feel porous and civic.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More complex and multi-winged than the candidate; useful as a sectional/public-space principle rather than a literal form.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, connected masses around a shared open space reinforce neighborhood-scale publicness and a coherent upper hierarchy.

warnings: The silhouette is somewhat conventional and could gain more section character without losing the dominant bent mass.
Access response is adequate but could be made more explicit at the ground edge.
Avoid over-fragmenting the mass into separate pieces; the current unity is a strength.
